newsitem.title: USA: Lockheed tops Pentagon list of defense firms.
newsitem.headline: Lockheed tops Pentagon list of defense firms.

text.p: Aerospace giant Lockheed Martin Corp last year again led all U.S. defence contractors with $12 billion in prime military contract awards, the Defence Department said on Friday.
In the Pentagon's annual list of firms ranked by prime contract totals, Lockheed led in fiscal 1996 for the second consecutive year, followed again by McDonnell Douglas Corp with $3.2 billion.
Rounding out the top five were General Motors Corp at $3.2 billion, Raytheon Co. with $3 billion and General Dynamics Corp. with $2.7 billion.

The merger of Lockheed and Martin Marietta in 1995 formed by far the nation's biggest defence contractor, but the currently proposed merger of McDonnell and Boeing poses a challenge to Lockheed's standing.

Lockheed, which garnered $10.5 billion in contract awards in fiscal 1995, builds a wide range of weaponary from the F-16 fighter jet to missiles, helicopters and electronics and communications equipment.

McDonnell was second on the list in 1996 for the second year in a row after increasing its contract awards to $9.9 billion from $8 billion in 1995. General Motors vaulted to third on the 1996 list from fourth place in the previous year.

Rounding out the top 10 firms in 1996 were were Northrop Grumman Corp and United Technologies Corp. at $2.6 billion each, Boeing Co. and Litton Industries Inc. at $1.7 billion each, and General Electric Co. with $1.5 billion.

McDonnell had led the list for years before the creation of Lockheed Martin in 1995, one of a number of major military industrial mergers which have consolidated the U.S. defence industry since the end of the Cold War.

U.S. military spending on arms has dipped in the past five years, and the Pentagon and other federal agencies are keeping a tight watch on big mergers, to prevent antitrust violations and to see that monopolies on arms manufacturing do not drive up the price of weapons.
